client-mu-plugins.description: Client must-use plugins. This is where the contents of mu-plugins belong on VIP.

images.description: Static images committed with the codebase, such as favicons and icons.

languages.description: Translation files. On VIP these are committed rather than generated at runtime.
languages.guidance: Plugins that write .mo files at runtime, such as WPML, cannot generate them here. Build them locally and commit the result.

plugins.description: Installed plugins, deployed from the application repository.

private.description: Files that are deployed but never served over HTTP.

themes.description: Installed themes, deployed from the application repository.

docs.description: Project documentation committed alongside the code.

mu-plugins.description: VIP reserves mu-plugins for its own platform code.
mu-plugins.guidance: Move the contents into client-mu-plugins/. Drop anything supplied by a previous host, such as the WP Engine mu-plugins.

blogs.dir.guidance: Move the media into uploads/, search-and-replace the stored paths, and add redirects for the old URLs. VIP only serves media from uploads/.

advanced-cache.php.guidance: Remove it. VIP installs its own drop-ins and provides a globally distributed edge cache.

object-cache.php.guidance: Remove it. VIP supplies a managed object cache backed by Memcached.

db.php.guidance: Remove it. VIP runs HyperDB and does not permit alternative database drop-ins.

debug.log.guidance: Do not commit it. The application directory is read-only on VIP, so nothing can append to it there.

wflogs.guidance: Remove it along with Wordfence. VIP provides platform-level security monitoring, and Wordfence is on the VIP incompatibility list.

w3tc-config.guidance: Remove it along with W3 Total Cache, which is on the VIP incompatibility list.

ai1wm-backups.guidance: Remove it. VIP takes platform-level backups and All-in-One WP Migration is on the VIP incompatibility list.

uploads.description: Media library. On VIP this is mapped to the VIP File System object store.
uploads.guidance: Do not commit it. Media is imported separately with the VIP CLI. This is the one path under wp-content that application code may write to.

upgrade.description: Temporary directory WordPress uses while installing updates.
upgrade.guidance: Local only. It is not deployed, and VIP applies updates through the repository instead.

upgrade-temp-backup.description: Temporary rollback copies created by the WordPress updater.
upgrade-temp-backup.guidance: Local only, and safe to delete.

cache.description: Cache directory written by a caching or optimisation plugin.
cache.guidance: Nothing can write here on VIP. Identify the plugin that owns it and remove or reconfigure it; the platform edge cache replaces it.

fonts.description: Font files, typically written by the WordPress font library.
fonts.guidance: Commit fonts with the theme instead of relying on a writable wp-content/fonts directory.

index.php.description: Empty index file WordPress ships to prevent directory listing.
index.php.guidance: Harmless. VIP serves through NGINX and does not rely on it.

.htaccess.guidance: VIP serves requests through NGINX, so this file is ignored. Re-express redirects in vip-config.php or a redirect plugin, and access rules in application code.

.phpcs.xml.dist.description: PHP_CodeSniffer configuration, used by the VIP Code Analysis Bot.

.vipgoci_phpcs_skip_folders.description: Folders excluded from the VIP Code Analysis Bot PHPCS scan.

incompatible.all-in-one-wp-migration: Backup and migration plugin. VIP performs platform-level backups, and this plugin writes archives into wp-content.
incompatible.wp-all-import: Import tooling that conflicts with the VIP import pipeline and needs write access outside uploads.
incompatible.wp-all-import-pro: Import tooling that conflicts with the VIP import pipeline and needs write access outside uploads.
incompatible.wp-all-export: Export tooling that conflicts with the VIP backup infrastructure.
incompatible.wp-all-export-pro: Export tooling that conflicts with the VIP backup infrastructure.
incompatible.w3-total-cache: Page caching plugin. Not designed for the VIP globally distributed edge cache, and it writes config and cache files into wp-content.
incompatible.wp-fastest-cache: Page caching plugin that writes cache files to a read-only filesystem.
incompatible.wp-rocket: Page caching plugin built around Apache and .htaccess. VIP serves through NGINX.
incompatible.wp-super-cache: Page caching plugin that conflicts with the built-in VIP page cache.
incompatible.wp-smushit: Image optimisation plugin with observed incompatibilities against the VIP File System.
incompatible.sucuri-scanner: Security plugin that conflicts with VIP security infrastructure.
incompatible.wordfence: Security plugin that requires filesystem writes and conflicts with VIP security infrastructure.
incompatible.wp-file-manager: Browses and edits files in the WordPress install. The VIP application filesystem is read-only, so edits silently fail.

caution.contact-form-7: Versions before 5.8.1 require filesystem write access. Confirm the installed version and test file uploads.
caution.gravityforms: Attempts filesystem writes outside uploads. Widely used on VIP in practice — test entry storage and file uploads before deciding.
caution.sitepress-multilingual-cms: WPML writes .mo files into wp-content/languages, which is read-only on VIP. Generate the language files locally and commit them.
caution.tablepress: Needs write access for imports and exports. Verify against the uploads directory.
caution.ninja-tables: Needs write access for imports and exports. Verify against the uploads directory.
caution.wpdatatables: Needs write access for imports and exports. Verify against the uploads directory.
caution.wpforms: Writes uploads and logs. Confirm every path resolves inside the uploads directory.
caution.wpforms-lite: Writes uploads and logs. Confirm every path resolves inside the uploads directory.
caution.elementor: Generates per-page CSS files and makes heavy use of the object cache. Both are performance risks on VIP.
caution.elementor-pro: Generates per-page CSS files and makes heavy use of the object cache. Both are performance risks on VIP.
caution.advanced-custom-fields: Supported, but field groups should be stored as JSON committed with the theme rather than in the database.
caution.advanced-custom-fields-pro: Supported, but field groups should be stored as JSON committed with the theme rather than in the database.
caution.buddypress: Avatar and cover-photo handling iterates upload directories and calls opendir()/closedir(), which fatals on the VIP File System.
caution.buddyboss-platform: Shares the BuddyPress avatar handling that fatals on the VIP File System.
caution.amazon-s3-and-cloudfront: WP Offload Media diverts uploads away from the VIP File System, which produces broken or empty thumbnails.

redundant.wp-parsely: Provided by the VIP platform as a must-use plugin.
redundant.redis-cache: VIP supplies a managed object cache. A second object-cache drop-in conflicts with it.
redundant.litespeed-cache: Page caching is handled by the VIP edge cache.
redundant.autoptimize: VIP concatenates and minifies CSS and JavaScript at the platform level.
redundant.wp-optimize: Combines caching and database optimisation, both of which VIP manages.
redundant.breeze: Page caching is handled by the VIP edge cache.
redundant.comet-cache: Page caching is handled by the VIP edge cache.
redundant.cache-enabler: Page caching is handled by the VIP edge cache.
redundant.hummingbird-performance: Page caching and asset optimisation are handled by the VIP platform.
redundant.wp-crontrol: VIP runs scheduled events through Cron Control.
redundant.application-passwords: Merged into WordPress core in 5.6 and no longer needed as a plugin.
